Aether Pharmaceuticals - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only portions. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are David Thornton, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Thornton, CEO of Aether Pharmaceuticals.

David Thornton, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Aether Pharmaceuticals delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust demand for our blockbuster oncology asset Aethrozin, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody that's solidified an 18% U.S. market share in non-small cell lung cancer, and the continued ramp-up of our GLP-1 agonist GlucoMax amid surging interest in obesity and diabetes treatments. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including accelerating our late-stage pipeline, optimizing our commercial execution in a complex reimbursement environment, and maintaining operational discipline to fuel innovation.

Let me start with our regulatory approvals and label expansions achieved this quarter, which represent some of the most transformative milestones in our history. We secured four major wins across our portfolio, unlocking an estimated $1.2 billion in incremental peak sales potential by 2027. This builds on the evolving immuno-oncology and rare disease landscapes where we're gaining substantial ground.

Our flagship Aethrozin earned FDA approval for its supplemental new drug application in first-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC patients with PD-L1 TPS of 1% or higher, in combination with carboplatin-pemetrexed. This expands from our prior second-line approval, where it's already driving $450 million in quarterly U.S. sales, up 42% year-over-year, and growing our addressable U.S. patient population from 25,000 to 68,000 annually. The Phase III ZENITH-301 data showed a 28% PFS improvement with a hazard ratio of 0.72 and a 22% OS benefit at 0.78, with Grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events at just 14%, on par with leading combos. Pricing remains at about $185,000 per patient-year, and we expect 35% U.S. uptake within a year. The EMA followed suit with approval for the same expansion, adding 22,000 EU5 patients and €320 million in peak sales, while Japan's PMDA is slated for Q1 2025 under SAKIGAKE fast-track.

In rare diseases, our AAV9-based gene therapy AetherGene for Duchenne muscular dystrophy in ambulatory boys aged 4-7 with exon 51-skipping amenable mutations received full FDA traditional approval. Pivotal MYO-201 trial results demonstrated 67% of patients achieving over 25% microdystrophin expression at week 64 versus zero in controls, plus 4.2-point gains on the North Star Ambulatory Assessment. Priced at $2.8 million per one-time dose, aligning with payer precedents like Sareptar's Elevidys, we're targeting 1,200 initial U.S. patients for $180 million in year-one sales ramping to $900 million peak. UK MHRA conditional approval via ILAP and China NMPA acceptance are in motion.

HEMA-FUSE, our bispecific T-cell engager for multiple myeloma, got frontline expansion for high-risk patients post-induction with pomalidomide-dex, based on FUSE-302's 52% ORR versus 32% control and 14.3-month duration of response. This adds $350 million to our U.S. forecast, lifting share to 22%. EU CHMP positive opinion looms in Q4. Finally, DERMA-STAT's pediatric approval in Canada for ages 12-plus in atopic dermatitis boosts our global opportunity to 4.2 million patients.

These achievements lift our FY2024 revenue guidance by 15% to $3.85-$3.95 billion, with gross margins up 300 basis points to 82% on biologics mix. Our 90% Phase III success rate, powered by AI patient stratification, outshines industry norms, and six more filings are under review.

Turning to our strategic priorities and outlook, we're focused on three pillars: pipeline acceleration, commercial optimization, and operational excellence. Our R&D investment hit $575 million in Q2, over 25% of revenues, prioritizing oncology, rare diseases, and metabolics.

Aethrozin posted $1.1 billion in sales, up 22%, with frontline NSCLC and HCC expansions on deck—Phase III HCC readout Q4 2024 for $6.5 billion peak potential. Our ADC ONC-512 hits Phase II completion soon, with AI from NVIDIA boosting ORR to 65%+. AetherGene advances with RMAT for BLA by year-end 2025 at $2.8 billion peak, alongside CRISPR beta-thalassemia. GlucoMax grabbed 15% GLP-1 share, $450 million sales, 28% weekly script growth; obesity readout Q1 2025 unlocks $10 billion TAM, backed by Singapore scale-up.

Biosimilars like UST-101 launch EU Q4 for $1.2 billion peak. Commercially, U.S. (62% sales) holds pricing steady at 48% gross-to-net via formulary wins; Europe (22%) grows 12% via IEHP; Asia-Pacific (12%) surges 32% on China JV. Ops savings of $250 million YTD cut COGS 300 bps; M&A dry powder at $4.5 billion post-AuraGene deal; dividend up 25% to $0.80/share, $2 billion buybacks.

We're raising FY24 guidance to $9.2-9.5 billion revenue (15-18% growth), non-GAAP EPS $7.85-8.15; FY25 $11.0-11.5 billion (19-22%), EPS $9.50-9.90. Diversified blockbusters with 2030+ exclusivity de-risk us.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen, our CFO, for detailed financials.

Lisa Chen, CFO:
Thank you, David. As David highlighted, we had a solid quarter. Revenue reached $2.5 billion, up 25% year-over-year, primarily from Aethrozin's $1.2 billion contribution—fueled by 25% U.S. volume growth and label expansions into MSI-high endometrial cancers—and GlucoMax's $350 million ramp, with gross margins expanding 400 basis points to 88% on efficiencies.

GAAP net income was $650 million, or $2.10 per share. Non-GAAP net income stood at $850 million, or $2.75 per share.

Operating expenses totaled $1.1 billion, reflecting heavy R&D reinvestment—$1.2 billion year-to-date across 12 Phase 3 assets—while maintaining discipline. Our cash position remains strong at $2.8 billion in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments, up 28% from year-end 2023 and 12% sequentially.

Let me expand on our cash flow and balance sheet highlights, which highlight our core strength and capital discipline. Our current ratio is 2.8x, topping industry medians; inventory up 15% QoQ to $450 million for GlucoMax launch and EU H2 approval, eyeing 500,000 Q3 units. Debt is modest at $1.1 billion—3.25% convertibles due 2028 and $300 million Takeda term loan—yielding $1.7 billion net cash, negative 0.8x net debt to EBITDA. Intangibles at $3.2 billion from GeneX acquisition; PP&E up 22% YoY to $1.5 billion on Singapore biologics expansion.

Operating cash flow set a record at $950 million, up 32% YoY and 18% QoQ, excluding $150 million R&D tax credit for $825 million non-GAAP. Royalties from Takeda added $120 million; DSO improved to 52 days. Free cash flow was $620 million after $330 million capex (10-12% of revenue): 55% GlucoMax scale to 200,000 liters, 30% AI discovery with Insilico, 15% AetherGene-HBB trials. Investing outflows $420 million on CAR-T milestones and China ADC stake; financing $50 million from ESPP, $300 million YTD buybacks at $45/share.

U.S. 65% of flows, Europe 22%, EM 10% up 45% YoY on Shanghai JV. FY24 OCF $3.4-3.6 billion, FCF $2.0-2.2 billion, net cash >$2.0 billion.

On pricing and reimbursement, we've adeptly managed headwinds. U.S. (62% sales) saw ASP stable at $145,000 for Aethrozin despite IRA, with 78% formulary coverage via outcomes rebates; GTN at 47% from 340B/PAP, offset by $120 million assistance. WAC hikes 5.2%. Europe: GeneX premium €2.1 million in Germany, NICE risk-sharing UK; ex-U.S. ASP flat, 12 new wins. China NRDL 62% discount drove 45% growth; Japan C2 pricing. Initiatives include RWE with Flatiron, outcomes contracts (25%), biosimilar launches, global corridors at 55-65% U.S. WAC. FY24 GTN 46-48%, ex-U.S. pricing +3-5%.

For full year, guidance now revenues $9.2-9.5 billion, EPS $7.85-8.15.

Now, I'll hand back to David.

David Thornton, CEO:
Thank you, Lisa. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David or Lisa, on the recent Aethrozin label expansion, how do you see uptake playing out given the competitive frontline NSCLC space with Keytruda and Tecentriq? And any update on manufacturing for the expanded volumes?

David Thornton, CEO:
Thanks, Emily. Great question. We're projecting strong uptake based on ZENITH-301's superior PFS and OS data, positioning Aethrozin as a differentiated PD-1/VEGF bispecific. Symphony analogs suggest 35% share within 12 months at parity pricing. Sales force expansion and payer wins are key. On manufacturing, our Singapore facility is at 120% utilization but $400 million capex keeps us ahead, with 200,000-liter bioreactor capacity matching Lilly's scale for GlucoMax too. Dr. Patel can add if needed.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Emily, the safety profile—14% Grade 3/4 TRAEs—gives confidence in combo adoption. Real-world registry data from 50,000 patients will support further expansions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Reilly with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mark Reilly, JPMorgan:
Lisa, your FCF guidance looks robust at $2.0-2.2 billion—how much is baked into M&A optionality, and thoughts on radiopharma bolt-ons like Point Biopharma? Also, on GlucoMax obesity label, any payer feedback?

Lisa Chen, CFO:
Mark, thanks. FCF yield supports 20%+ R&D reinvestment and bolt-ons; $4.5 billion dry powder eyes ADCs and radiopharma to complement Aethrozin in solid tumors. We've hedged 70% 2025 forex for Japan royalties. On GlucoMax, payers are receptive given 88% margins and script momentum—formulary wins with CVS/Express project 20-25% Type 2 share, with obesity readout de-risked for Q1 2025.

David Thornton, CEO:
To add, Mark, our Shanghai JV and Fosun partnership unlock EM growth, with NRDL driving China volumes.

Operator:
Our next question from Sophia Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sophia Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. On gene therapies like AetherGene and AetherGene-HBB, how are you addressing payment-over-time models and capacity? And regional diversification amid IRA reference pricing?

Lisa Chen, CFO:
Sophia, we're adopting annuity structures like Lilly's donanemab—$400-500K annualized—to ease uptake, with UK NICE and German AMNOG precedents. North Carolina AAV facility hits 120% utilization, but $200 million capex ensures scale. Diversification: U.S. 65%, EU 20% via adaptive pathways, EM 10-15% by 2026 on BRICS harmonization and China CDE filings.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Efficacy data—67% microdystrophin expression—plus RMAT/ORPHAN designations fast-track this, akin to Zolgensma but with better CNS penetration.

Operator:
Our final question from Alex Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim, Bank of America:
Quick one on biosimilars—UST-101 EU launch timing and U.S. interchangeability path? And capex breakdown sustainability?

Lisa Chen, CFO:
Alex, UST-101 EMA-approved, Q4 EU launch targets $1.2 billion peak as Stelara patents cliff; U.S. data H1 2025 for interchangeability. Capex at 10-12% sustainable: 55% GlucoMax, 30% AI/Insilico platform, 15% trials—yielding high-single-digit FCF on EV.

David Thornton, CEO:
Thanks, Alex. Biosimilars offset originator erosion while we lead in bispecifics and gene editing.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

David Thornton, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Aether Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
